claims.text: Isothermal aging of a single-phase magnetic high-entropy alloy can induce nanoscale precipitates.
The induced nanoscale precipitates act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Precipitate-induced domain-wall pinning increases the coercive field relative to an as-cast or homogenized baseline.
A homogenized, single-phase ferromagnetic FCC or BCC high-entropy alloy can provide a uniform starting microstructure with negligible secondary precipitates.
Aging at approximately 650°C for approximately 10 hours can precipitate a minor coherent secondary phase.
An inert atmosphere prevents oxidation during the aging treatment.
Sufficient solute supersaturation is required for the selected aging treatment to produce uniform nanoscale precipitation.
The selected aging treatment must avoid overaging and precipitate coarsening for the proposed effect to hold.
Dispersed nanoscale precipitates create local strain fields and variations in magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Local strain fields and magnetocrystalline-anisotropy variations pin magnetic domain walls.
The precipitates impede domain-wall motion during magnetization reversal.
Greater resistance to domain-wall motion produces a higher coercive field.
The aged alloy will exhibit a statistically significant increase in room-temperature coercive field relative to the matched baseline.
The magnitude of coercivity enhancement depends on aging kinetics and precipitate density.
The coercivity enhancement requires aging that avoids significant grain growth or overaging.
The coercivity enhancement requires the matrix to retain robust magnetic ordering during heat treatment.
